newsitem.title: SENEGAL: European Union and Senegal fishing talks fail.
newsitem.headline: European Union and Senegal fishing talks fail.

text.p: The European Union and Senegal have failed to agree on conditions for renewing their two-year fishing agreement, sources close to the talks say.
The failure to strike a deal meant all European Union trawlers had to leave Senegalese waters by Friday. No fresh talks were planned before 1997, sources from both sides said.
Senegal was demanding a payment of 18 million ECUs while the European Union was offering only 10 million ECU.
"We failed to reach agreement," one European delegate told Reuters, adding that relations between the two side in trade and other areas were unaffected.
The accord expired on October 1 but was extended until October 31 pending fresh talks. A total of 14 European fishing boats were in Senegalese waters before the talks collapsed.
Senegal's minister of fisheries and transport, Alassane Dialy Ndiaye, said at the start of the talks that failure to agree would not herald disaster for the fishing industry.
"If an accord is not signed in the immediate future that will probably cause some disruption but I don't think that will result in the end of fishing in Senegal," he said.
The European Union gave Senegal 31.2 million ECU for 1992-94 and 15.8 million ECU for 1994-96.
The fishing industry earned Senegal more than 137 billion CFA francs in 1995. More than 400,000 people depend on the industry directly or indirectly for the livelihood.
